text: The project needs a default voice so that we can at least ship it with one working voice. This is a project that I've been making to see how generative AI can work completely locally.
It's been a very interesting project actually because I've noticed that we can make a lot of things that exist online in subscription form and we can just run that locally.
The game that I've made with this system is called Overtime, and actually this is almost completely Claude's work, if I'm honest.
So I basically gave Claude access to this project and it was able to generate 3D assets, it generated music, dialogue, textures, animations even, so rigged animations, and all of this is
an attempt at being state-of-the-art as close as possible to subscription-based models.
I don't think that generative AI has absolutely no place in the future. I think it will have a place.
I also think it's completely up to the people to decide whether they do or do not want to consume generative AI content, so...
I think it's very important to have, like, disclosure so that people know, okay, real humans worked on this, or I actually would rather have, I'm okay with generative AI.
If you wonder what my stance is on the whole thing, honestly, I don't know, right?
As a creative I'm obviously very worried about being replaced and like not just not being able to do my work anymore or my work just being
But I also think that there is potential and keep in mind that the Overtime game is something that was made.
with very little creative input and it was almost completely Claude, with some minor requests from me but
It does beg the question if somebody who was a creative used these tools and actually used them seriously, how would that turn out?
There is one problem that I have with this idea though, is that I feel like GenAI is addicting.
It kind of works like a slot machine where you don't really know what's gonna come out and if something good comes out that's great but you have little control over the process.
I have some future plans to try and deal with this and try to make it so that GenAI games don't feel like slop.
I think it's generally important that people have input in what GenAI outputs.
The thing what we refer to as slop is simply the baseline of what AI can produce with little human input.
It is low effort. It is basically like making a game yourself and just having a square that moves around on the screen with nothing else going on.
I'm not saying that we can adopt GenAI, but I do think that we should at least consider it and try it.
Honestly, I feel like if you have tried it and it sucks, then you have a good argument not to use it. And then all of this is just going to blow over.
